get.description:
Follow-up actions, those about ``ref`` (``asset:<id>``) when given: an app shows what was
decided about the asset it is showing (docs/collaboration.md). Read only. A person's token
reads the actions that person sees; an app's service token reads them all.

schema.title: Response Actions Api V1 Actions Get

get.description: ``PLANTCRAFT_APPS`` and the apps installed from the Apps page (docs/app-package.md).

schema.title: Response Apps Api V1 Apps Get

get.description:
The app's runtime (a zip of its Python packages) that runs its objects on the person's
computer or in their browser.
The objects of one kind, as the app lists them for this person (``plantcraft-objects/1``).

post.description:
Ask the app to run one object (``run = "app"``): the app starts it in its own queue, with
the person's access, when its administrator allows notebook runs; read back what it
answers in ``started`` (``{"kind": "run", "id": ...}``).

get.description: One object, whole: what a notebook needs to read it or run it.

post.description: Call one app's tool with the person's identity; the app's answer comes back as it is.

get.description: The type catalog with inherited attributes and roles resolved.

schema.title: Response Asset Types Api V1 Asset Types Get

get.description:
``kind`` is the exact type; ``type`` also takes its subtypes. Result assets (what apps
record about assets) come only with ``results=true`` or when asked by type. ``limit`` and
``cursor`` answer it in pages by id; an ``ETag`` answers a list that did not change with
304 (``plantcraft_sdk.server.paging``).

schema.title: Response Assets Api V1 Assets Get

put.description:
An app's whole set of result assets (``{"assets": [...]}``, see ``parse_result_assets``).

Only a service token, for its own app (403 otherwise); a broken item makes the request a
422 and nothing is written. Results no longer listed are ended, not removed.
``{"saved", "ended"}``.

schema.title: Response Put Result Assets Api V1 Assets Results Put

post.description:
An app removes result assets of its own (``{"ids": [...]}``); others' ids are skipped.
Their points stay in the Historian until their retention ends. ``{"removed"}``.

schema.title: Response Remove Result Assets Api V1 Assets Results Remove Post

Every declared event, PlantCraft's first: ``[{"app", "name", "events", "undeclared"}]``,

The events an app declares (its ``[[publishes.events]]``), replaced; sent by the SDK

What the Queue panel lists for this person, from the runs apps write: ``mine`` (what

``{"me", "mine", "running"}``; each run as ``GET /api/v1/runs`` gives it, with ``app_name``.

schema.title: Response Queue Api V1 Queue Get

get.description:
The latest results; ``under`` keeps the results about an asset and the assets under
it, ``group`` (an asset type, e.g. ``unit``) adds the ancestor of that type to each.

In pages of at most ``limit`` (``MAX_PAGE``) results by subject, app and kind: when more
are left the answer has an ``X-Next-Cursor`` header, and ``?cursor=`` reads on. Before
pages, a list cut at 5,000 said nothing: 1,000 bench loops filled it and the assistant
never saw the plant's signals (2026-10-27).

schema.title: Response Results Api V1 Results Get

put.description: Write up to 500 results; each failing item is in ``errors``, the rest are saved.

schema.title: Response Put Results Api V1 Results Put

schema.title: Response Result History Api V1 Results History Get
Response Runs Api V1 Runs Get

put.description: Write up to 500 runs (one per app and run id); failing items are in ``errors``.

schema.title: Response Put Runs Api V1 Runs Put
Response Schedules Api V1 Schedules Get

schema.title: Response Put Schedules Api V1 Schedules Put

post.description:
Many signals' series in one request and one source read; each failure is listed
in ``errors`` (404, 422, 502, or 413 when the request ran out of points).

schema.title: Response Series Batch Api V1 Series Post

put.description:
Derived series: an app's service token writes computed series to ``app-<app id>``.

The whole body is checked first (422); an item naming another app's source makes the
request a 403 and nothing is written. ``{"written", "errors"}``.

schema.title: Response Put Series Api V1 Series Put

post.description:
An app retires derived series it no longer writes (``{"signals": [...]}``).

Only its own source (403 otherwise, nothing retired). A retired series is no longer listed
nor read; the Historian keeps its archive for its retired days. ``{"retired", "errors"}``.

schema.title: Response Retire Series Api V1 Series Retire Post

put.description:
Runs points: an app's service token writes one whole series per execution
(``[{"signal", "run_at", "t", "v", "keep_runs", "keep_days", ...}]``) to ``app-<app id>``.

Checked as ``PUT /api/v1/series`` is (422, then 403 for another app's source, nothing
written). A run at the same ``run_at`` replaces it. ``{"written", "errors"}``.

schema.title: Response Put Series Runs Api V1 Series Runs Put

get.description:
Every signal; ``app``, ``subject`` and ``result`` keep the derived signals that have them.
``limit`` and ``cursor`` answer it in pages by id; an ``ETag`` answers a list that did not
change with 304.

schema.title: Response Signals Api V1 Signals Get

get.description: One signal by id; a bare tag one source has answers that signal (deprecated).

schema.title: Response Signal Api V1 Signals  Signal Id  Get

get.description:
The executions a runs point keeps: ``{"signal", "runs": [{"run_at", "start", "end",
"n"}]}``, newest first; 422 for another kind.

schema.title: Response Run List Api V1 Signals  Signal Id  Runs Get

get.description:
Recorded values, or one mean (text: the last label) per ``step`` seconds; at most
200,000 points. ``signal`` in the answer is the id as asked. A runs point answers
``{"signal", "kind": "runs", "runs": [{"run_at", "t", "v"}]}``, newest first: the run at
``run`` (``latest`` by default, or its ISO time) or the ``runs`` newest.

schema.title: Response Series Api V1 Signals  Signal Id  Series Get

get.description:
One aggregate (``last, mean, min, max, std``) over the ``window`` that ends now.

A text signal has only ``last``, its newest label.
